items.en: Reformare meant 'to form again, reshape'; Christian writers used it of souls being remade in virtue, so the moral sense is as old as the word.
items.cn: reformare 意为「再次成形、重塑」；教父作家用它指灵魂在德性中被重造，可见道德义与这个词一样古老。

items.en: Old French reformer carried the verb into Romance daily use, covering both reshaping things and reshaping conduct.
items.cn: 古法语 reformer 把该动词带入罗曼语的日常使用，兼指重塑事物与重塑品行。

items.en: The verb is recorded in English around 1300 in the sense 'to convert into a better state'; the personal sense 'to restore from sin' follows in the same century.
items.cn: 动词约在 1300 年已见于英语，义为「使进入更好的状态」；「使人脱离罪恶」的个人义同一世纪出现。

items.en: The noun reform, the political movement sense, and the labels Reformation and reformer establish the word at the centre of public life.
items.cn: 名词 reform、政治运动义，以及 Reformation（宗教改革）与 reformer（改革者）等标签，使这个词坐上公共生活的中心。

note.en: The first group gathers the formare 'shape' family with different prefixes. The second group compares the words for making something better by deliberate change.
note.cn: 第一组汇集 formare「塑造」词族配上不同前缀的词。第二组比较「通过有意的改变使某物变好」的词。

entries.definition: the act of reforming, or the great sixteenth-century religious movement. The noun of the process.
entries.definitionCN: 改革行为，或十六世纪的宗教改革运动。过程的名词。

entries.definition: a person who works to change a system or a bad habit. It names the shaper, not the shape.
entries.definitionCN: 致力于改变制度或恶习的人。它命名塑造者，而非形状。

entries.definition: literally to shape within, hence to give knowledge or shape to a mind.
entries.definitionCN: 字面是「在内塑形」，引申为赋予知识、启迪心智。

entries.definition: to change the shape completely, across from one kind to another. Transform goes further than reform.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底改变形状，从一种变为另一种。transform 的改变幅度大于 reform。

entries.definition: to shape oneself together with a standard, to fit in.
entries.definitionCN: 使自身与标准同形，即遵从、顺应。

entries.definition: to make better in quality without implying structural change. Improve adds value; reform rebuilds shape.
entries.definitionCN: 在品质上变好，不隐含结构改变。improve 增值；reform 重塑形。

entries.definition: to examine and repair thoroughly, often of machines or systems. Overhaul stresses the full taking-apart.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底检修，多用于机器或制度。overhaul 强调全面拆解。

entries.definition: to correct faults in a text or law, usually by small changes. Amend patches; reform reshapes.
entries.definitionCN: 修正文本或法律中的缺陷，通常是小改动。amend 是打补丁；reform 是重塑。

entries.definition: to organize the parts of a system or company again. It stresses the skeleton rather than the faults.
entries.definitionCN: 重新组织制度或公司的结构。它强调骨架，而非弊端。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin re- 'again' + formare 'to shape', the family reformation, reformer, transform and conform, and the picture of casting a new shape.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 re-「再」加 formare「塑造」，词族 reformation、reformer、transform、conform，以及浇铸新形状的图景。

normal.en: re- means again and formare means to shape: reform is giving something a second shape.
normal.cn: re- 是「再」，formare 是「塑造」：reform 就是给某物第二次形状。

normal.en: Form, formal, format and reform all carry the same Latin shape-word.
normal.cn: form、formal、format、reform 都带着同一个拉丁「形状」词。

normal.en: Transform reshapes across kinds; reform reshapes to remove faults; conform reshapes to fit.
normal.cn: transform 跨类重塑；reform 去弊重塑；conform 顺应重塑。

normal.en: Reformation with a capital R names the sixteenth-century religious movement.
normal.cn: 大写 R 的 Reformation 专指十六世纪宗教改革运动。

normal.en: The verb works on laws and on people alike: both can be cast in a new shape.
normal.cn: 这个动词对法律和对人同样有效：两者都能被浇铸成新形状。

abstract.en: Picture a foundry: the old casting is broken up, the metal is melted, and a better shape is poured.
abstract.cn: 想象一间铸造厂：旧铸件被打碎，金属熔化，更好的形状被浇铸出来。

abstract.en: Reform keeps the material and changes the form: nothing new is added, only the shape is replaced.
abstract.cn: reform 保留材质、更换形状：不添加新东西，只是替换形状。

abstract.en: A person who reforms melts down old habits and pours new ones into the same life.
abstract.cn: 改过自新的人熔掉旧习惯，把新的浇进同一段人生。

examples.en: The education ministry began to reform the national curriculum last year.
examples.cn: 教育部去年开始改革国家课程。

examples.en: Many hoped the young offender would reform after serving his sentence.
examples.cn: 许多人希望那个少年犯服刑后能改过自新。

examples.en: Health care reform dominated the whole election campaign.
examples.cn: 医疗改革主导了整场竞选。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞福姆」——瑞福把走形的模具「扶」正，重新「模」塑一遍 → reform 改革；改过自新（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 reformare「再次塑造」（re- 再 + formare 塑造），核心是「保留材质、重塑形状以去弊求好」。

sensesIntro.en: Seven senses of reform, all around one act: shaping again — a system, a practice, or a life is melted down and given a better form.
sensesIntro.cn: reform 的七个义项都围绕同一行为：再次塑造——一个制度、一种做法或一段人生被熔炼，并被赋予更好的形状。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a new shape cast over the same material, faults removed.
core.cn: 核心意象：在同一材质上浇出新形状，去掉毛病。

chain: LET THE PERSON HARDEN INTO IT

branches.en: SYSTEMS AND PRACTICES: laws and habits alike are reshaped fault by fault.
branches.cn: 制度与做法：法律与习惯同样被一处一处地重塑。

branches.en: PEOPLE: the shaping turns outward on offenders, or reflexive when a person changes himself.
branches.cn: 人：塑造既可外向作用于犯过者，也可自反——一个人重塑自己。

branches.en: PLAIN RE-FORMING: a broken party or line simply forms again, without any judgement of faults.
branches.cn: 朴素再造：解散的政党或队伍只是再次成形，不涉及任何弊端评判。

branches.en: THE PLAN: the noun names the new shape before it is poured, as a public proposal.
branches.cn: 方案：名词在浇铸之前就命名了新形状，作为公开的提案。

branches.en: THE RESULT: after hardening, the noun names the improved life itself.
branches.cn: 结果：凝固之后，名词命名的是那段变好了的人生本身。

intro.en: Reform carries the Latin prefix re- 'again' on the stem formare 'to shape'. The formare family is one of the widest in English: form, formal, format, inform, transform, conform, deform and perform all share it.
intro.cn: reform 在词干 formare「塑造」上带有拉丁前缀 re-「再」。formare 词族是英语最庞大的词族之一：form、formal、format、inform、transform、conform、deform、perform 都出自它。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is reformare (re- 'again' + formare 'form, shape'), from forma 'shape, figure'. Formare also gives French former and Italian formare with the same meaning.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语源头是 reformare（re-「再」+ formare「塑造」），出自 forma「形状」。formare 也生成了法语 former 与意大利语 formare，词义相同。

items.meaning: to shape again; to make better by reshaping
items.meaningCN: 改革；改造（re- 再 + formare 塑造）
items.example: They voted to reform the courts.
items.exampleCN: 他们投票改革司法系统。

items.meaning: the process of reforming; the religious movement
items.meaningCN: 改革；宗教改革运动（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: The reformation of the tax code took years.
items.exampleCN: 税法改革历时数年。

items.meaning: a person who reforms
items.meaningCN: 改革者（-er 表示施动者）
items.example: She is remembered as a great social reformer.
items.exampleCN: 她作为伟大的社会改革家被铭记。

items.meaning: supporting gradual reform rather than revolution
items.meaningCN: 改良主义的（主张渐进改革而非革命）
items.example: The reformist wing won the party vote.
items.exampleCN: 党内改良派赢得了投票。

items.meaning: to shape the mind with facts; to tell
items.meaningCN: 告知；启迪（in- 在内 + formare 塑造）
items.example: Good journalism informs the public.
items.exampleCN: 好的新闻启迪公众。

items.meaning: to change the shape entirely
items.meaningCN: 使彻底改变（trans- 横越 + formare 塑造）
items.example: The railway transformed the region.
items.exampleCN: 铁路彻底改变了这个地区。

items.meaning: to shape oneself to a standard
items.meaningCN: 遵从；符合（con- 一起 + formare 塑造）
items.example: All products must conform to safety rules.
items.exampleCN: 所有产品必须符合安全规定。

items.meaning: to spoil the shape of
items.meaningCN: 使变形；损毁外形（de- 离去 + formare 塑造）
items.example: Heat deformed the plastic frame.
items.exampleCN: 高温使塑料框架变形。

items.meaning: following an agreed outward shape
items.meaningCN: 正式的；形式上的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The invitation asked for formal dress.
items.exampleCN: 请柬要求着正装出席。

items.meaning: to carry a task fully into shape; to do
items.meaningCN: 执行；表演（per- 彻底 + formare 塑造）
items.example: The team performed well under pressure.
items.exampleCN: 团队在压力下表现出色。

definition_zh: 冰箱；冷藏箱；冷冻室
definition_en: a machine or box that keeps food cold so that it stays fresh, or the cold compartment inside it
core_image: 一只沉默的白色大箱子，日夜把箱里的热抽走，让牛奶和青菜都睡在凉气里
scene: 深夜的厨房里只有这台机器在低声嗡嗡作响，灯一亮，冷气扑面而来。He tiptoed to the refrigerator for a glass of cold milk.
sceneCN: 这里 refrigerator 是「冰箱」（第 1 个义项：冷藏食物的机器）；句意：他踮着脚走到冰箱前取一杯冷牛奶。场景要点：深夜厨房、机器的嗡嗡声、打开时的灯光与冷气。

pos.zh: 冰箱；冷藏箱；冷冻室

collocations.phrase: put the leftovers back in the refrigerator

derivatives.zh: 同根动词，义为「冷藏；使冷却」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「制冷；冷藏；冷藏技术」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「制冷剂」
由 refrigerator 截短而来的口语词，义为「冰箱」

senses.title: The machine that keeps food cold
senses.definition: a household appliance that cools and stores food so that it stays fresh for days
senses.definitionCN: 家用制冷并储存食物的电器，使食物保鲜数天
senses.example: The refrigerator hums all night in the corner of the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 冰箱整夜在厨房角落里嗡嗡作响。
senses.why: The name says what it does: it makes cold — refrigerare is to make cool again, and the box does it day and night.
senses.whyCN: 名字直接说出它的功能：制造寒冷——refrigerare 意为「再度降温」，这只箱子日夜在做这件事。

senses.title: The cold compartment itself
senses.definition: the inner compartment of a refrigerator where the food is kept, as in take it out of the refrigerator
senses.definitionCN: 冰箱内部存放食物的隔间，如说「从冰箱里把它拿出来」时所指的空间
senses.example: There is half a melon in the refrigerator.
senses.exampleCN: 冷藏室里有半个甜瓜。
senses.why: The machine's name came to name its cold inside: the place stands for the cooling.
senses.whyCN: 机器的名字转而命名它冰凉的内部：这个空间就成了「制冷」的代名词。

senses.title: Any cooling box or device
senses.definition: any box, room, or vehicle fitted to keep things cold, such as a cold store or a refrigerated truck body
senses.definitionCN: 任何被装设成低温的箱子、库房或车厢，如冷库或冷藏车厢
senses.example: The laboratory refrigerator holds the vaccine samples.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室的冷藏箱存放着疫苗样品。
senses.why: Once cooling, not the kitchen, is the point, the word travels to labs, ships, and stores.
senses.whyCN: 当要点从厨房变成「制冷」，这个词便走向实验室、轮船与仓库。

intro.en: Refrigerator comes from the verb refrigerate, from Latin refrigerare 'to make cool again', from re- 'again' + frigare 'to be cold', a form related to frigere 'to be cold'. The household machine sense belongs to the age of electricity.
intro.cn: refrigerator 出自动词 refrigerate，上溯拉丁语 refrigerare「再度降温」，由 re-「再」加 frigare「变冷」构成，frigare 与 frigere「寒冷」相关。家用机器义属于电气时代。

items.en: The reconstructed root *sneigwh- or related cold roots give Latin frigus 'cold' and English frost, freeze, frigid. The family of cold is old and wide.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 *sneigwh- 及相关的寒冷词根生成了拉丁语 frigus「寒冷」与英语 frost、freeze、frigid。「寒冷」家族古老而庞大。

items.en: Refrigerare meant 'to make cool again, to refresh', used literally of weather and food, and figuratively of refreshing the spirit.
items.cn: refrigerare 意为「使再度凉爽、使精神振作」，既实指天气与食物，也比喻振奋心神。

items.en: The verb refrigerate is recorded in English by the early sixteenth century, first in learned and medical contexts of cooling the body or a fever.
items.cn: 动词 refrigerate 到十六世纪初已见于英语，最早用于学术与医学语境，指为身体或高热降温。

items.en: Refrigeratory and refrigerator first name any cooling vessel or room for ice; ice boxes did the work in ordinary homes.
items.cn: refrigeratory 与 refrigerator 最初指任何冷却的器皿或储冰的房间；普通家庭靠冰盒完成同样的工作。

items.en: The electric household refrigerator spread from the 1910s and 1920s; the clipped form fridge arose in the twentieth century and became the everyday word.
items.cn: 电冰箱自二十世纪一二十年代起普及；截短形式 fridge 也在二十世纪出现，成为日常用语。

note.en: The first group gathers the cold family built on Latin frigus and the clipped forms of the machine. The second group compares the containers and machines that keep food.
note.cn: 第一组汇集以拉丁语 frigus 与机器截短形式构成的寒冷词族。第二组比较保存食物的容器与机器。

entries.definition: the everyday short form of refrigerator, standard in British English speech and now everywhere.
entries.definitionCN: refrigerator 的日常截短形式，英式口语标准词，现已通行各地。

entries.definition: the process or technology of keeping things cold. It names the science, not the box.
entries.definitionCN: 制冷过程或技术。它命名这门技术，而不是那只箱子。

entries.definition: the working fluid inside the cooling machine that carries heat away.
entries.definitionCN: 制冷机内部带走热量的工作流体。

entries.definition: formally very cold, of weather or manner. A cold word from the same Latin family, without any box.
entries.definitionCN: 正式用语「严寒的」，形容天气或态度。同一拉丁词族的冷词，与箱子无关。

entries.definition: an older name for a cooling room or vessel, now only of historical interest.
entries.definitionCN: 冷却室或冷却容器的旧称，今仅具历史意义。

entries.definition: the compartment or machine kept below freezing point. Freezer freezes solid; refrigerator merely cools.
entries.definitionCN: 低于冰点的隔间或机器。freezer 结冻；refrigerator 只降温。

entries.definition: an insulated box cooled by a block of ice, the predecessor of the electric refrigerator.
entries.definitionCN: 靠冰块降温的隔温箱，电冰箱的前身。

entries.definition: a portable insulated box for keeping food cold on a trip, without power.
entries.definitionCN: 旅行用的便携隔温箱，无需电源。

entries.definition: a large building kept cold for storing food in bulk, the industrial cousin of the household machine.
entries.definitionCN: 大批量储存食物的大型低温建筑，是家用机器的工业表亲。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin re- 'again' + frigare 'to be cold', the family refrigerate, refrigeration, refrigerant and frigid, and the clipped form fridge.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 re-「再」加 frigare「变冷」，词族 refrigerate、refrigeration、refrigerant、frigid，以及截短形式 fridge。

normal.en: re- means again and frigare means to be cold: the machine makes the inside cold again and again.
normal.cn: re- 是「再」，frigare 是「变冷」：这台机器一次次把箱内变冷。

normal.en: Frigid and refrigerator share the cold root; one is the weather, the other the box.
normal.cn: frigid 与 refrigerator 同一寒冷词根：一个是天气，一个是箱子。

normal.en: English frost and freeze are native cousins of the same cold idea.
normal.cn: 英语本土的 frost 与 freeze 是同一「寒冷」观念的亲戚。

normal.en: The everyday word fridge comes from clipping the long word at both ends.
normal.cn: 日常词 fridge 来自把这个长词首尾截短。

normal.en: Refrigeration names the process, refrigerant the fluid, refrigerator the box: three levels of the same cooling.
normal.cn: refrigeration 是过程，refrigerant 是流体，refrigerator 是箱子：同一制冷的三个层面。

abstract.en: Picture a white box that breathes the opposite way of a fire: it drinks heat out of everything inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一只白箱子，呼吸方式与火相反：它把箱内一切的热喝掉。

abstract.en: Open the door at night: the little lamp, the puff of cold air, the hum that never stops.
abstract.cn: 夜里打开门：小小的灯、扑面的冷气、永不停歇的嗡嗡声。

abstract.en: A refrigerator is a private winter that keeps your milk alive.
abstract.cn: 冰箱是一片私人寒冬，替你把牛奶保鲜。

examples.en: The milk should stay in the refrigerator until you need it.
examples.cn: 牛奶用之前要一直放在冰箱里。

examples.en: Their new refrigerator is quiet and uses very little power.
examples.cn: 他们的新冰箱很安静，耗电也少。

examples.en: She labeled every container before it went back into the refrigerator.
examples.cn: 每个容器放回冰箱前她都贴了标签。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞福瑞记瑞特」——瑞福家的冰箱会「瑞」着自己「记」得天天制冷，特别尽职 → refrigerator 冰箱（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 refrigerare「再度降温」（re- 再 + frigare 变冷），核心是「反复把热抽走、维持低温」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of refrigerator, all the same machine seen from outside, inside, and far away: the appliance, its cold compartment, and any cooling box built on the same idea.
sensesIntro.cn: refrigerator 的三个义项是同一台机器的三个视角：作为电器的它、它冰凉的内部，以及遵循同一构想的各种冷藏装置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a box that draws heat out and keeps an inner winter.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只把热抽走、在内部维持寒冬的箱子。

chain: THE COMPARTMENT STANDS FOR THE COLD
LABS AND TRUCKS KEEP COOL TOO

branches.en: THE APPLIANCE: the kitchen machine that hums day and night.
branches.cn: 电器：日夜嗡嗡作响的厨房机器。

branches.en: THE INSIDE: the cold space itself, where the melon waits.
branches.cn: 内部：冰凉的空间本身，甜瓜就在那里等着。

branches.en: THE IDEA EVERYWHERE: labs, ships, and stores borrow the name for their own cold boxes.
branches.cn: 构想普及：实验室、轮船与仓库也借这个名字称呼各自的冷箱。

branches.en: SCALE: from one kitchen box to a warehouse of cold, the cooling idea is the same at every size.
branches.cn: 尺度：从厨房一只箱到一座冷库，制冷构想在任何规模上都相同。

branches.en: BY METONYMY: the name of the machine slides onto the space and onto anything that makes such a space.
branches.cn: 转喻：机器之名滑向空间本身，再滑向一切能造出这种空间之物。

intro.en: Refrigerator carries the Latin prefix re- 'again' on the stem frigare 'to be cold', with the agent-like noun ending -or, here meaning 'the thing that does it'. The cold family also gives frigid, frigidarium and English frost, freeze.
intro.cn: refrigerator 在词干 frigare「变冷」上带有拉丁前缀 re-「再」，并加类施动者名词词尾 -or，此处意为「做这件事的东西」。寒冷词族还给出 frigid、frigidarium 以及英语 frost、freeze。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is refrigerare 'make cool again' (re- 'again' + frigare 'be cold'), from frigus 'cold'. Roman frigidarium was the cold room of a bathhouse, the oldest relative of the kitchen box.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语源头是 refrigerare「再度降温」（re-「再」+ frigare「变冷」），出自 frigus「寒冷」。罗马的 frigidarium 是浴场中的冷水间，是厨房冷箱最古老的亲戚。

items.meaning: the box that makes cold
items.meaningCN: 冰箱（re- 再 + frigare 变冷 + -or 施动者）
items.example: Put the bottle back in the refrigerator.
items.exampleCN: 把瓶子放回冰箱。

items.meaning: to make cold; to preserve by cold
items.meaningCN: 冷藏；冷冻保存（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: Refrigerate the dough overnight.
items.exampleCN: 把面团冷藏一夜。

items.meaning: the process or industry of cooling
items.meaningCN: 制冷；冷藏（技术）（-ion 构成过程名词）
items.example: Modern refrigeration changed the food trade.
items.exampleCN: 现代制冷改变了食品贸易。

items.meaning: the fluid that carries heat away in a cooling machine
items.meaningCN: 制冷剂（-ant 表示起作用的物质）
items.example: Old refrigerants harmed the ozone layer.
items.exampleCN: 旧式制冷剂曾破坏臭氧层。

items.meaning: the everyday word for a refrigerator
items.meaningCN: 冰箱（refrigerator 的截短口语形式）
items.example: The fridge is almost empty again.
items.exampleCN: 冰箱又快空了。

items.meaning: formally very cold
items.meaningCN: 严寒的；冷淡的（-id 构成形容词）
items.example: A frigid wind came off the mountains.
items.exampleCN: 寒风从山那边吹来。

items.meaning: the cold room of a Roman bath
items.meaningCN: 浴场冷水间（-arium 表示场所）
items.example: Bathers cooled off in the frigidarium.
items.exampleCN: 浴客在冷水间里纳凉。

items.structure: Old English frost, same cold family
items.meaning: ice crystals formed by freezing weather
items.meaningCN: 霜（英语本土寒冷词，与拉丁词族为远亲）
items.example: Frost covered the field at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 清晨的田野覆满了霜。

items.structure: Old English freosan, same cold family
items.meaning: to turn into ice; to become very cold
items.meaningCN: 结冰；冻结（英语本土寒冷词）
items.example: The lake froze in the first week of January.
items.exampleCN: 湖在一月第一周结了冰。

items.meaning: kept cold by machine
items.meaningCN: 冷藏的；冷冻运输的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: The vaccines travelled in a refrigerated truck.
items.exampleCN: 疫苗由冷藏卡车运送。

definition_zh: 拒绝；拒收；不肯；拒给；废物；垃圾；废料
definition_en: to say no to an offer, request, or thing offered, or the waste material that is thrown away
core_image: 一只手把手推了回去：请求与赠物到了门前，被原路送走；被送走的残渣堆在屋后
scene: 服务员递上一杯酒，他轻轻按住了杯沿，示意自己一滴也不能沾。She refused the glass of wine politely.
sceneCN: 这里 refuse 是「拒绝接受」（第 1 个义项：对送到面前的东西说不）；句意：她礼貌地拒绝了那杯酒。场景要点：餐桌、递来的杯子、轻轻按住的杯沿。

pos.zh: 拒绝；拒收；不肯给
拒绝
废物；垃圾；废料

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「拒绝；拒绝的表示」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「拒绝者」（较少用）
由名词加名词构成的复合词，义为「垃圾堆；垃圾场」

senses.title: Say no to something offered
senses.definition: to decline to accept or take something that is offered or given
senses.definitionCN: 对送来或给予的东西表示不接受、不收下
senses.example: She refused the glass of wine politely.
senses.exampleCN: 她礼貌地拒绝了那杯酒。
senses.why: The Latin fundere means 'to pour': something poured or offered toward you is poured back, sent away from your door.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 fundere 意为「倾倒」：向你倒来、递来的东西被倒回去，被送离你的门前。

senses.title: Say no to do something
senses.definition: to say firmly that you will not do something, followed by to and a verb
senses.definitionCN: 坚决表示不愿做某事，后接 to 加动词
senses.example: The witness refused to answer the question.
senses.exampleCN: 证人拒绝回答这个问题。
senses.why: Here what is poured back is the request itself: it reaches you and is returned unopened.
senses.whyCN: 这里被退回的是请求本身：它到达你这里，又被原封不动地送回。

senses.title: Not give what is asked for
senses.definition: to not grant something that someone asks you to give, such as permission, money, or information
senses.definitionCN: 对别人请求给予的东西不予提供，如许可、钱或信息
senses.example: The bank refused her a second loan.
senses.exampleCN: 银行拒绝给她第二笔贷款。
senses.why: The thing asked for is like water in your hand: refusing pours nothing out, the hand stays closed.
senses.whyCN: 所求之物如你手中的水：拒绝就是一滴不倒，手保持合拢。

senses.title: Keep someone or something out
senses.definition: to not allow a person or thing to enter or pass, as in refuse entry
senses.definitionCN: 不允许某人或某物进入或通过，如 refuse entry
senses.example: The guards refused the reporters entry to the building.
senses.exampleCN: 警卫拒绝记者进入大楼。
senses.why: Movement toward the inside is stopped at the boundary: the poured stream is turned back at the door.
senses.whyCN: 向内的移动在边界处被截住：倾来的水流在门口被折返。

senses.title: Waste material thrown away
senses.definition: rubbish or waste matter, especially the mixed solid waste collected from homes and streets
senses.definitionCN: 垃圾或废弃物，尤指从住户和街道收集的混合固体垃圾
senses.example: City trucks collect the household refuse every Tuesday.
senses.exampleCN: 市政卡车每周二清运生活垃圾。
senses.why: What has been refused and thrown out takes the name of the act: refuse is the poured-away stuff.
senses.whyCN: 被拒绝、被丢弃的东西承袭了动作的名字：refuse 就是「被倒掉的东西」。

senses.title: Leftovers of a process
senses.definition: the worthless remainder left after a manufacturing or natural process, such as sawdust or cane fibre
senses.definitionCN: 制造或自然过程后留下的无价值残余，如锯末、甘蔗渣
senses.example: The mill burns the cane refuse to power itself.
senses.exampleCN: 糖厂燃烧甘蔗废料为自身供电。
senses.why: The industrial sense keeps the image of what falls out of the stream of good output and is poured aside.
senses.whyCN: 工业义保留这一图景：好产品流出后掉队的东西，被倒在一旁。

intro.en: Refuse (verb) comes from Old French refuser, of uncertain ultimate origin, generally traced to Latin refutare 'to repel, refute' or to a Vulgar Latin reflex of refundere 'to pour back', from re- 'back' + fundere 'to pour'. The noun refuse 'rubbish' grew from the verb in the fifteenth century.
intro.cn: 动词 refuse 来自古法语 refuser，更早出处不确定，一般追溯到拉丁语 refutare「击退、驳斥」，或 Vulgar Latin 中 refundere「倒回」的形式（re-「回」+ fundere「倾倒」）。名词 refuse「垃圾」于十五世纪由动词衍生。

items.en: The reconstructed root *gheu- 'to pour' underlies Latin fundere 'to pour', English found and fuse (melt). Pouring is the shared picture.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 *gheu-「倾倒」生成了拉丁语 fundere「倾倒」与英语 found、fuse（熔化）。共同的图景是「倒出」。

items.en: Refutare meant 'to repel an attack, refute'; refundere meant 'to pour back'. Both show the same motion: something comes toward you and is driven or poured back.
items.cn: refutare 意为「击退、驳斥」；refundere 意为「倒回」。两者显示同一动作：某物朝你而来，被击退或倒回去。

items.en: Refuser appears in Old French meaning 'to reject, refuse'; its exact path from the Latin verbs is debated among etymologists.
items.cn: refuser 在古法语中出现，意为「拒绝、拒收」；它与上述拉丁动词之间的确切演变路径在词源学家中仍有争议。

items.en: The verb is recorded in English in the fourteenth century, meaning 'to decline to accept, deny'.
items.cn: 动词十四世纪已见于英语，意为「拒收、否认」。

items.en: The noun refuse 'rubbish, waste' appears in the fifteenth century; the pronunciation of the noun with a stressed first syllable distinguishes it from the verb.
items.cn: 名词 refuse「垃圾、废物」出现于十五世纪；名词重音在前，以此与动词区分。

note.en: The first group gathers words of the pour-back family and the look-alike refute, which is a different verb with the same shape. The second group compares the verbs of saying no and the words for waste.
note.cn: 第一组汇集「倒回」词族以及形似的 refute——后者是同形状的另一个动词。第二组比较「说不」的动词与「废物」的名词。

entries.definition: the act or statement of refusing. It is the noun of the verb, keeping its stress.
entries.definitionCN: 拒绝的行为或表示。是动词的名词形式，保留动词重音。

entries.definition: to prove a claim wrong. It looks like refuse and may share the Latin refutare, but it means winning an argument, not saying no.
entries.definitionCN: 证明某一说法有误。它与 refuse 形似、可能同出 refutare，但指在论辩中驳倒，而非拒绝。

entries.definition: shelter from danger. It comes from fugere 'to flee', not from fundere; only the spelling is close.
entries.definitionCN: 躲避危险的庇护所。出自 fugere「逃」，与 fundere 无关，只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: to pour money back, hence to return payment. It keeps the literal pouring.
entries.definitionCN: 把款项倒回去，即退款。它保留了「倾倒」的本义。

entries.definition: to pour things together until they mix, hence to mix up in the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西倒在一起使其混淆，引申为使心智混乱。

entries.definition: to refuse politely, especially an invitation or offer. Decline is the courteous form of refusing.
entries.definitionCN: 礼貌地拒绝，尤指邀请或提议。decline 是 refuse 的客气版。

entries.definition: to throw a thing back as unfit. Reject judges the thing; refuse may refuse without judging.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物当作不合格而退回。reject 带评判；refuse 可以不加评判。

entries.definition: to refuse to give or admit, or to declare untrue. Deny works on requests and statements.
entries.definitionCN: 拒给、不承认，或宣称不实。deny 作用于请求与说法。

entries.definition: household waste, chiefly American usage. Garbage and refuse name the same kitchen bin by different roads.
entries.definitionCN: 生活垃圾，多为美式用法。garbage 与 refuse 从不同路径命名同一只厨房垃圾桶。

entries.definition: material that is unwanted or unused. Waste is broader: it covers what is never even offered for use.
entries.definitionCN: 无用或未用的物料。waste 范围更广，连从未被拿来使用的东西也算。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin re- 'back' + fundere 'to pour', the family refund, confuse, refusal and refute, and the two-stress pattern that separates verb and noun.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 re-「回」加 fundere「倾倒」，词族 refund、confuse、refusal、refute，以及区分动名词的重音模式。

normal.en: re- means back and fundere means pour: refusing pours the offer back out the door.
normal.cn: re- 是「回」，fundere 是「倾倒」：refuse 就是把递来的东西倒出门外。

normal.en: Refund is the literal pour-back: your money returns the way it came.
normal.cn: refund 是字面的「倒回」：钱原路退回。

normal.en: Confuse pours many things into one pot: the result is a mixed-up mind.
normal.cn: confuse 把许多东西倒进一锅：结果就是一团乱麻的头脑。

normal.en: The verb is reFUSE, the noun is REfuse: stress keeps them apart.
normal.cn: 动词重音在后 reFUSE，名词重音在前 REfuse：重音把它们分开。

normal.en: What is poured back out of the house ends up as refuse, the rubbish of the street.
normal.cn: 被从家里倒出来的东西，最终成了街头的 refuse（垃圾）。

abstract.en: Picture a closed door and a tilted jug: what is poured at the door runs back down the steps.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇关着的门和一只倾斜的壶：倒在门口的水顺台阶流了回去。

abstract.en: A refusal is a turned-out palm: nothing can land there.
abstract.cn: 拒绝是一只翻开的空手掌：什么也落不下来。

abstract.en: Refuse has two lives: one for the hand that says no, one for the bin that says good riddance.
abstract.cn: refuse 过着双重人生：一属于说「不」的手，一属于说「去得干净」的垃圾桶。

examples.en: He refused the invitation without giving a reason.
examples.cn: 他没有说明理由，拒绝了邀请。

examples.en: The engine refuses to start on cold mornings.
examples.cn: 冷天早晨这台发动机怎么也不肯启动。

examples.en: Separate the kitchen refuse from the paper and glass.
examples.cn: 把厨余垃圾与纸类、玻璃分开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞福尤斯」——瑞福端着一碗「油酥」摇头摆手：不肯收，转身倒掉 → refuse 拒绝；垃圾（只借音，不表词源）

root: 一般认为源自拉丁语 refundere「倒回」（re- 回 + fundere 倾倒）或 refutare「击退」，更早演变路径存疑；核心是「把朝你而来的东西送回去」。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses of refuse, all one motion seen twice: something arrives and is poured back — and what is poured back and thrown away becomes the rubbish named by the same word.
sensesIntro.cn: refuse 的六个义项是同一动作的两面：某物到达，被倒回去——而倒回去、丢弃掉的东西，就成了与动词同名的「垃圾」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand tilted like a jug, pouring what arrived back out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手像壶一样倾斜，把送来的东西倒出去。

chain: THE OUTSIDER STOPS AT THE DOOR

branches.en: THINGS AND GIFTS: offered things and asked-for things are both refused with the same closed hand.
branches.cn: 物品与给予：送来的与求来的东西，都被同一只合拢的手拒收。

branches.en: ACTIONS AND PEOPLE: a deed can be refused in advance, and a person can be refused at the boundary.
branches.cn: 行为与人：行为可被预先拒做，人可被拒在边界之外。

branches.en: THE BIN: what homes throw away is named by the verb itself, household refuse.
branches.cn: 垃圾桶：住户丢弃之物直接承袭动词之名，即生活垃圾。

branches.en: THE MILL: industry pours its worthless leftovers aside, and they too become refuse.
branches.cn: 工厂：工业把无价值的残余倒在一旁，它们同样成了废料。

branches.en: TWO STRESSES, ONE STORY: the verb says no at the door, the noun sweeps up after it.
branches.cn: 两种重音，一个故事：动词在门口说不，名词随后打扫。

intro.en: Refuse shows the prefix re- 'back' on the Latin stem fundere 'to pour'. The fundere family is rich in English: refund, confuse, diffuse, transfuse, suffice and fuse all pour in their own direction.
intro.cn: refuse 在拉丁词干 fundere「倾倒」上显示前缀 re-「回」。fundere 词族在英语中枝繁叶茂：refund、confuse、diffuse、transfuse、suffice、fuse 都朝着各自的方向「倾倒」。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is fundere 'to pour, melt', one of the most productive verbs; the verb refuse itself may also reflect refutare 'repel, refute', an origin still debated.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语源头是 fundere「倾倒、熔化」，是最高产的动词之一；动词 refuse 本身也可能反映 refutare「击退、驳斥」，其来源仍有争议。

items.meaning: to pour back an offer; waste matter
items.meaningCN: 拒绝；垃圾（re- 回 + fundere 倾倒）
items.example: She refused the bribe on the spot.
items.exampleCN: 她当场拒绝了贿赂。

items.meaning: the act of refusing
items.meaningCN: 拒绝（-al 构成行为名词）
items.example: His flat refusal ended the discussion.
items.exampleCN: 他断然拒绝，讨论就此结束。

items.meaning: to pour money back; a returned payment
items.meaningCN: 退款（把款项倒回去）
items.example: The shop refunded the full price.
items.exampleCN: 商店全额退款。

items.meaning: to pour together; to mix up
items.meaningCN: 使混乱；混淆（con- 一起 + fundere 倾倒）
items.example: The twins confused everyone at first.
items.exampleCN: 这对双胞胎起初让所有人分不清。

items.meaning: to pour out and spread in all directions
items.meaningCN: 扩散；散布（dis- 分开 + fundere 倾倒）
items.example: The smell of bread diffused through the house.
items.exampleCN: 面包的香味弥漫了整座房子。

items.meaning: to pour across, as blood into a patient
items.meaningCN: 输血；灌输（trans- 横过 + fundere 倾倒）
items.example: The surgeons transfused two units of blood.
items.exampleCN: 外科医生输了两个单位的血。

items.meaning: to pour up under, hence to be enough
items.meaningCN: 足够（sub- 在下 + fundere 倾倒，引申「够用」）
items.example: A short note will suffice.
items.exampleCN: 一张便条就够了。

items.meaning: to melt together; a safety wire that melts
items.meaningCN: 熔合；保险丝（出自分词 fusus）
items.example: The blown fuse darkened the whole flat.
items.exampleCN: 保险丝一断，整间屋子都黑了。

items.meaning: to prove wrong; to repel a claim
items.meaningCN: 驳斥；证明有误（refutare 击退）
items.example: The data refuted the earlier claim.
items.exampleCN: 数据驳斥了此前的说法。

items.meaning: a person who flees to safety
items.meaningCN: 难民（出自 fugere「逃」，与 refuse 词源不同）
items.example: The camp sheltered thousands of refugees.
items.exampleCN: 营地收容了数千名难民。

definition_zh: 看待；视为；注视；尊重；问候；关系；方面；关心
definition_en: to look at or think about someone or something in a stated way, to respect, or a look, greeting, respect, or connection
core_image: 一双眼睛停下来，久久望向对方：目光的停留变成心里的掂量，变成敬意或挂念
scene: 老人提起那位修桥的师傅时，眼里总有掩不住的敬意。He regarded the old bridge builder as a true craftsman.
sceneCN: 这里 regard 是「视为；看待」（第 2 个义项：把某人看作某种身份）；句意：他把那位老造桥人视为真正的匠人。场景要点：村口老桥、交谈的目光、交叠的双手。

pos.zh: 看待；视为；注视；尊重；注意
注视；尊重；问候；方面；关心

collocations.phrase: out of regard for her feelings

derivatives.zh: 由现在分词转介词，义为「关于；至于」
由动词加后缀构成，义为「不顾；不管怎样」
加否定前缀 dis- 构成，义为「漠视；不理会」
复数名词，义为「问候；致意」（信末客套语）

senses.title: Look steadily at something
senses.definition: to look at someone or something carefully and steadily
senses.definitionCN: 认真而长久地注视某人或某物
senses.example: She regarded the cracked ceiling for a long time.
senses.exampleCN: 她久久注视着那道开裂的天花板。
senses.why: The French garder means 'to watch, keep': to regard is to hold something with the eyes, guarding it with a look.
senses.whyCN: 法语 garder 意为「看守、照看」：regard 就是用眼睛「持有」某物，用目光看守住它。

senses.title: Think of someone as something
senses.definition: to consider or judge someone or something in a particular way, as in regard someone as something
senses.definitionCN: 以特定方式考虑或评判某人某物，用于 regard someone as… 结构
senses.example: The villagers regarded him as a lucky man.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们把他看作幸运的人。
senses.why: The look turns inward and becomes judgement: what the eyes hold, the mind labels.
senses.whyCN: 目光转向内心，变成评判：眼睛所持之物，心灵为其贴上标签。

senses.title: Respect or esteem someone
senses.definition: to think of someone with respect and honour
senses.definitionCN: 带着尊敬和敬意看待某人
senses.example: The whole school regarded her as its finest teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 全校都把她当作最好的老师来敬重。
senses.why: Holding a person steadily in mind, without letting go, is respect: the guarded look becomes guarded honour.
senses.whyCN: 把一个人稳稳放在心里不放，就是敬重：受看守的目光变成了受看护的敬意。

senses.title: A look or gaze
senses.definition: the act of looking at someone in a stated way, as in a cold regard
senses.definitionCN: 以某种方式注视的行为，如 a cold regard
senses.example: He met her cold regard without blinking.
senses.exampleCN: 他毫不眨眼地迎住她冰冷的目光。
senses.why: The noun keeps the original act: what the verb did, the noun can hold up for inspection.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留原始动作：动词做过的事，名词可以把它举起来供人审视。

senses.title: Respect or esteem as a thing
senses.definition: a feeling of respect for someone, as in hold someone in high regard
senses.definitionCN: 对某人的敬重之情，如 hold someone in high regard
senses.example: She is held in the highest regard by her colleagues.
senses.exampleCN: 她深受同事们的高度敬重。
senses.why: The look of respect becomes a possession of the heart, something one can hold high or lose.
senses.whyCN: 尊敬的目光变成心中的一件所有物，可以被高高捧起，也可能失去。

senses.title: A greeting at a distance
senses.definition: a message of respect sent to someone, especially in the plural at the end of a letter
senses.definitionCN: 送达某人的致意，尤以复数形式用于信末
senses.example: Give my regards to your family when you write.
senses.exampleCN: 写信时请代我向你家人问好。
senses.why: A look cannot travel, so a word is sent instead: the regard is a look carried by paper.
senses.whyCN: 目光无法送达，于是派词语代行：regard 成了由纸张携带的目光。

senses.title: Care or consideration for something
senses.definition: attention or care given to something, as in out of regard for, or without regard for
senses.definitionCN: 对某事的关注或顾及，用于 out of regard for 或 without regard for 等结构
senses.example: He drove without any regard for the icy road.
senses.exampleCN: 他开车完全不顾结冰的路面。
senses.why: To guard is to care: regarding the road is keeping it, and its danger, in mind.
senses.whyCN: 看守即是在意：顾及路面，就是把路面和它的危险都放在心里。

senses.title: A particular point or aspect
senses.definition: a specific respect in which something is considered, as in in this regard
senses.definitionCN: 考虑某事时的特定角度，如 in this regard
senses.example: The plan is cheaper, but in this regard it is also riskier.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案更便宜，但在这方面风险也更大。
senses.why: Each fixed gaze isolates one side of a thing: a regard is one direction of looking.
senses.whyCN: 每一次固定的注视都隔离出事物的一面：一个 regard 就是一个注视方向。

intro.en: Regard comes from Old French regarder 'to look back at, watch, consider', from re- 'back' + garder 'to guard, watch', itself of Germanic origin. The word moved from the eye to the mind and then to the letter's closing line.
intro.cn: regard 来自古法语 regarder「回望、注视、考虑」，由 re-「回」加 garder「看守、注视」构成，garder 源自日耳曼语。这个词从眼睛走向心灵，再走到信末的落款。

items.en: Garder descends from the Frankish *wardōn 'to watch, guard', related to English ward and warden. Watching and keeping are one act in this root.
items.cn: garder 源自法兰克语 *wardōn「看守、保卫」，与英语 ward、warden 相关。在这个词根里，「注视」与「看护」本是一件事。

items.en: Regarder meant 'to look back at, turn one's gaze to, take notice of'; the prefix re- adds the sense of turning the gaze back onto its object.
items.cn: regarder 意为「回望、把视线转向、注意」；前缀 re- 增加了「把目光折回对象」之意。

items.en: The verb appears in English in the fourteenth century, first meaning 'to notice, heed, look at'; the mental sense 'consider as' soon follows.
items.cn: 动词十四世纪进入英语，最初意为「注意、留心、注视」；「视为、考虑为」的心智义随后出现。

items.en: The noun senses of look, esteem, and greeting develop; the plural regards becomes the polite ending of letters.
items.cn: 名词的「目光」「敬意」「问候」诸义发展起来；复数 regards 成为书信的礼貌结尾。

items.en: The phrase in this regard treats the gaze as a direction of thought, and regardless makes the guarding fail: no gaze is kept on the thing at all.
items.cn: 短语 in this regard 把目光当作思维的一个方向；regardless 则让看护失效：对事物全然不加注视。

note.en: The first group gathers the garder 'watch' family, including its negation and its Germanic cousins. The second group compares the verbs of considering and the nouns of respect.
note.cn: 第一组汇集 garder「看守」词族，包括其否定形式与日耳曼表亲。第二组比较「考虑」类动词与「敬意」类名词。

entries.definition: about, concerning. The participle of regard turned into a little preposition.
entries.definitionCN: 关于、涉及。regard 的分词变成了一个小介词。

entries.definition: without paying attention, despite everything. It negates the guarding look.
entries.definitionCN: 不顾一切、不予理会。它否定了那道看护的目光。

entries.definition: to ignore deliberately, to fail to regard. Same family, opposite action.
entries.definitionCN: 蓄意忽视、不理会。同一词族，相反动作。

entries.definition: a keeper or guard, as of a prison or college. The Germanic member of the watching family.
entries.definitionCN: 看守人、管理人，如监狱或学院的。看守家族的日耳曼成员。

entries.definition: to keep safe by watching. It is the bare root behind regard.
entries.definitionCN: 看守、保卫。它是 regard 背后的朴素词根。

entries.definition: to think about carefully before deciding. Consider weighs; regard can be a settled view without weighing.
entries.definitionCN: 决定前仔细思考。consider 是称量；regard 可以是一个不需称量的既定看法。

entries.definition: to respect highly, or such respect itself. Esteem names the feeling; regard names it too, in a quieter register.
entries.definitionCN: 高度尊重，或这种尊重本身。esteem 命名这种情感；regard 以更平实的语体命名它。

entries.definition: to look at or think of in a stated way. View stresses the angle chosen; regard stresses the steadiness of the gaze.
entries.definitionCN: 以某种方式看待或注视。view 强调所选角度；regard 强调目光的稳定。

entries.definition: to admire someone's qualities, or such admiration. Respect looks up; regard simply looks and holds.
entries.definitionCN: 钦佩某人的品质，或这种钦佩。respect 是仰视；regard 只是注视并持守。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: French re- 'back' + garder 'to watch', the Germanic root behind guard, warden and ward, and the family regarding, regardless and disregard.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：法语 re-「回」加 garder「注视」，其日耳曼词根 guard、warden、ward，以及词族 regarding、regardless、disregard。

normal.en: regarder means to look back at: the gaze is turned and held on its object.
normal.cn: regarder 意为「回望」：目光被折回并停驻在对象上。

normal.en: garder is the cousin of guard: both mean to watch over and keep.
normal.cn: garder 是 guard 的表亲：都意为看护与保有。

normal.en: A warden keeps watch over a prison; a regard keeps watch over a person in the mind.
normal.cn: warden 看守监狱；regard 在心里看守一个人。

normal.en: Disregard and regardless both undo the watching: the look is dropped.
normal.cn: disregard 与 regardless 都撤除了注视：目光被丢弃。

normal.en: Kind regards at the end of a letter is a look sent through the post.
normal.cn: 信末的 kind regards 是由邮局代寄的一道目光。

abstract.en: Picture a sentry who never turns away: his standing watch is the word's oldest picture.
abstract.cn: 想象一名从不移开视线的哨兵：他的站立守望就是这个词最古老的图景。

abstract.en: To hold someone in high regard is to keep their picture on the top shelf of your mind.
abstract.cn: hold someone in high regard 就是把他的画像摆在你心灵的最高一格。

abstract.en: Every regard is a direction: once you fix one, you are no longer looking at the rest.
abstract.cn: 每个 regard 都是一个方向：一旦定住它，其余的便不再入眼。

examples.en: Critics regard the novel as her finest work.
examples.cn: 评论家们视这部小说为她最好的作品。

examples.en: He regarded the empty stage for a moment before speaking.
examples.cn: 开口前，他朝空荡的舞台注视了片刻。

examples.en: Please pass on my regards to the whole team.
examples.cn: 请代我向全队问好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞嘎的」——瑞福的目光「嘎」的一声定在老匠人身上，敬「的」不得了 → regard 注视；视为；敬意（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自古法语 regarder「回望、注视」（re- 回 + garder 看守），garder 上溯日耳曼语词根，与英语 guard、ward 同源，核心是「用目光看守」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of regard, all from one held gaze: the look itself, the judgement it carries, the respect it becomes, the greeting it sends, and the single direction it fixes on.
sensesIntro.cn: regard 的八个义项都来自一道持守的目光：目光本身、目光承载的评判、它化成的敬意、它捎去的问候，以及它定住的那个单一方向。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gaze that stops, holds, and keeps watch over what it sees.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道停下、持住并守望所见的目光。

chain: A WORD CARRIES THE LOOK AFAR

branches.en: THE LOOK: the verb watches and the noun holds the watching up for inspection.
branches.cn: 注视：动词在守望，名词把这份守望举起来供人审视。

branches.en: JUDGEMENT: the held gaze yields a label, and each label is one fixed direction of thought.
branches.cn: 评判：持住的目光产出标签，而每个标签都是思维的一个固定方向。

branches.en: RESPECT: the verb esteems, the noun is the esteem that can be held high.
branches.cn: 敬意：动词表示敬重，名词则是可以高高捧起的敬意。

branches.en: GREETING: when distance defeats the gaze, words carry the look instead.
branches.cn: 问候：距离使目光失效时，便由词语代为携带目光。

branches.en: CARE: guarding the object in mind is caring for it; dropping the gaze is disregard.
branches.cn: 关心：在心里看护对象就是在意它；丢掉目光便是 disregard。

intro.en: Regard adds the prefix re- 'back' to garder 'to watch', a French form of the Germanic root behind guard, ward, warden and warder. The family runs from the sentry's post to the end of a letter.
intro.cn: regard 在 garder「注视」上添加前缀 re-「回」；garder 是日耳曼词根的法语形式，guard、ward、warden、warder 都出自它。这个词族从哨兵的岗位一直延伸到信末落款。

latinIntro.en: Strictly, the root is Germanic rather than Latin: Frankish *wardōn 'to watch' became Old French garder. English borrowed the word twice — as guard from French and as ward from Germanic sources.
latinIntro.cn: 严格说，这个词根属于日耳曼而非拉丁：法兰克语 *wardōn「看守」演变为古法语 garder。英语两次借入——经法语借来 guard，经日耳曼语源保有 ward。

items.meaning: to watch steadily; to consider as; respect
items.meaningCN: 注视；视为；尊重（re- 回 + garder 看守）
items.example: She regarded the letter with suspicion.
items.exampleCN: 她满腹疑虑地看着那封信。

items.meaning: about, concerning
items.meaningCN: 关于（分词转介词）
items.example: He said nothing regarding the incident.
items.exampleCN: 对于那次事件他什么也没说。

items.meaning: without attention or hindrance
items.meaningCN: 不顾；不管怎样（-less 表示「没有」）
items.example: They marched on regardless of the rain.
items.exampleCN: 他们不顾下雨继续前进。

items.meaning: to ignore deliberately
items.meaningCN: 漠视；不理会（dis- 离去 + regard）
items.example: The court disregarded the unsigned evidence.
items.exampleCN: 法庭未采信未签署的证据。

items.structure: French borrowing of the same root
items.meaning: to keep watch over; a protector
items.meaningCN: 看守；卫兵（同一词根的法语借入形式）
items.example: Two guards stood at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 两名卫兵守在门口。

items.meaning: an official who keeps watch over a place
items.meaningCN: 看守人；管理员（日耳曼 ward + -en）
items.example: The traffic warden waved us on.
items.exampleCN: 交通管理员挥手让我们通过。

items.meaning: a guarded district; a person under guard, as a hospital patient
items.meaningCN: 病房；受监护人（古英语 weard，同根）
items.example: She spent the night in the children's ward.
items.exampleCN: 她在儿科病房过了一夜。

items.meaning: greetings, especially at a letter's end
items.meaningCN: 问候；致意（regard 的复数）
items.example: With best regards, Maria.
items.exampleCN: 谨致问候，玛丽亚。

items.meaning: concern for oneself; self-respect or vanity
items.meaningCN: 自我关注；自尊或自恋（self- 自身 + regard）
items.example: His constant self-regard tires his friends.
items.exampleCN: 他无休止的自我关注让朋友疲惫。

items.meaning: a legal keeper of a person or rights
items.meaningCN: 监护人；保护者（guard + -ian）
items.example: Her uncle acted as her legal guardian.
items.exampleCN: 她的叔叔担任她的法定监护人。

definition_zh: 政权；统治制度；管理体制；养生法；训练方案
definition_en: a government or system of ruling a country, or a planned way of living, eating, or training
core_image: 一整套按固定刻度运转的规程：国家用它统治，身体用它作息
scene: 铁栅门开了又关，喇叭里每天定点传出同样的通告。Life under the old regime was strict and silent.
sceneCN: 这里 regime 是「政权；统治制度」（第 1 个义项：统治国家的一套体制）；句意：旧政权治下的生活严苛而沉默。场景要点：高墙、喇叭、整齐的脚步声。

pos.zh: 政权；统治制度；管理体制；养生法；训练方案

forms.label: 复数（多种体制、多个方案）

derivatives.zh: 同源近亲词，义为「养生法；疗程；作息制度」（更强调规则本身）
同源词，义为「团（军队编制）；纪律约束」（作动词指严格管束）
同前缀词，义为「地区的；区域的」（出自 regere 的领域概念）
同根动词，义为「管理；调节；管制」

senses.title: A government that rules
senses.definition: a government, especially one that rules in a particular or forceful way
senses.definitionCN: 一个政府，尤指以特定或强势方式执政的政府
senses.example: The old regime collapsed after weeks of protest.
senses.exampleCN: 旧政权在数周抗议后垮台。
senses.why: The Latin regere means 'to rule, guide straight': the regime is the hand on the reins of a country.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 regere 意为「统治、引直」：regime 就是握着一国缰绳的那只手。

senses.title: The system and style of rule
senses.definition: the method, system, or period during which a particular government or style of governing holds power
senses.definitionCN: 特定政府或执政方式掌权的方法、制度或时期
senses.example: Scholars still study the economic policies of that regime.
senses.exampleCN: 学者们仍在研究那个时期的各项经济政策。
senses.why: Ruling is not just holding power but steering it: the system of steering, like the run of a racehorse, takes the same name.
senses.whyCN: 统治不只是握权，更是驾驭：这套驾驭体系，如赛马的奔跑步法，用的是同一个名字。

senses.title: A managed system in an organization
senses.definition: a system of managing or controlling an organization, activity, or area
senses.definitionCN: 管理或控制某机构、活动或领域的体系
senses.example: The industry operates under a strict licensing regime.
senses.exampleCN: 该行业在严格的许可制度下运营。
senses.why: Any ruled domain is a little state: the same straightening hand governs prices, licences, or machines.
senses.whyCN: 任何被治理的领域都是一个小国：同一只「引直」之手管着价格、执照或机器。

senses.title: A planned routine for the body
senses.definition: a planned set of rules for diet, exercise, or medical treatment, followed regularly
senses.definitionCN: 为饮食、锻炼或治疗而制订、定期遵守的一套规则
senses.example: He follows a strict regime of swimming and stretching every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他每天早上严格执行游泳加拉伸的训练方案。
senses.why: The body, like the state, is ruled by a straightening hand: rules for eating and exercise hold the body to its line.
senses.whyCN: 身体如同国家，也由一只「引直」之手治理：饮食与锻炼的规则把身体保持在线上。

intro.en: Regime comes from French régime, from Latin regimen 'rule, guidance, steering', from regere 'to rule, to keep straight'. Latin regimen covered both the reins of a horse and the discipline of a body, and modern English has inherited the double use.
intro.cn: regime 来自法语 régime，上溯拉丁语 regimen「统治、指导、驾驭」，出自 regere「统治、保持笔直」。拉丁语 regimen 既指马的缰绳，也指身体的规训，现代英语继承了这双重用法。

items.en: The reconstructed root *h3reg- 'to move in a straight line, to direct' underlies Latin regere, English right, reckon and rich, all picture a straight guiding hand.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 *h3reg-「直线行进、引导」生成了拉丁语 regere 与英语 right、reckon、rich——都画着一只「引直」之手。

items.en: Regimen meant 'the act of steering, rule, discipline', used of government and of health rules alike; regere also gives regula 'a straight bar, rule'.
items.cn: regimen 意为「驾驭、统治、规训」，既用于政务也用于健康规则；regere 还派生 regula「直杆、规则」。

items.en: French régime carried both senses: the style of government and the ordered way of living, especially diet and discipline.
items.cn: 法语 régime 兼有两义：执政风格，以及有次序的生活方式，尤指饮食与规训。

items.en: The word enters English first as the diet-and-health sense; the political sense 'particular government' grows in the eighteenth century, often of foreign governments.
items.cn: 该词先以「饮食养生」义进入英语；「特定政府」的政治义在十八世纪成长，常指外国政权。

items.en: The political use becomes dominant in journalism, often with a critical flavour; the sense of any managed system, from taxes to training, spreads widely.
items.cn: 新闻语体中政治义渐成主导，常带批评色彩；从税收制度到训练计划，「任何受管体系」的用法广泛铺开。

note.en: The first group gathers the regere 'rule straight' family, where regimen and regiment share the same Latin shape with different fates. The second group compares the words for systems of rule.
note.cn: 第一组汇集 regere「引直统治」词族，regimen 与 regiment 同形异命。第二组比较「统治体系」类词。

entries.definition: a prescribed course of diet, exercise, or treatment. It stresses the rules; regime can name the rulers themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 规定的饮食、锻炼或疗程。它强调规则；regime 可指统治者本身。

entries.definition: a military unit of a thousand or so soldiers; as a verb, to control people too strictly. Same straightening root, pointed at soldiers.
entries.definitionCN: 约千人的军队编制单位；作动词指过度管束。同一「引直」词根，指向士兵。

entries.definition: to control by rules, keeping something working straight. The verb behind the regime.
entries.definitionCN: 用规则管制，使运转保持笔直。是 regime 背后的动词。

entries.definition: a person who rules in place of a monarch, as a child king's stand-in.
entries.definitionCN: 代君主执政的人，如幼年国王的替手。

entries.definition: a large area of land. The ruled district of the same root: what the straightening hand governs.
entries.definitionCN: 大片陆地。同一词根的「辖区」：被引直之手治理的地方。

entries.definition: the body that governs a country. Government is the neutral word; regime often implies judgement on how it rules.
entries.definitionCN: 治理国家的机构。government 是中性词；regime 常隐含对其执政方式的评判。

entries.definition: the executive part of a government, often named for its leader. It stresses running the machine, not the style of ruling.
entries.definitionCN: 政府的行政分支，常以其领导人命名。它强调运转机器，而非执政风格。

entries.definition: an organized set of rules or methods. System has no hand on the reins; regime always implies one.
entries.definitionCN: 有组织的规则或方法体系。system 没有握缰之手；regime 总是暗含一只。

entries.definition: a usual sequence of actions. Routine is what one drifts into; a regime is planned and imposed.
entries.definitionCN: 惯常的行为序列。routine 是自然养成的；regime 是被规划并强加的。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin regere 'to rule, keep straight', the family regimen, regiment, regulate and region, and the reins-in-hand picture.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 regere「统治、保持笔直」，词族 regimen、regiment、regulate、region，以及「手握缰绳」的图景。

normal.en: regere means to keep straight: a ruler keeps a country on the line, as reins keep a horse.
normal.cn: regere 意为「保持笔直」：统治者让国家走在线上，如同缰绳管住马。

normal.en: Regimen and regime are the same Latin word in two English rooms: one for rules, one for rulers.
normal.cn: regimen 与 regime 是同一个拉丁词住进英语的两间屋：一间放规则，一间放统治者。

normal.en: Regiment, the soldiers' unit, carries the same root: troops ruled into straight lines.
normal.cn: 军队编制 regiment 同根：士兵被治成笔直的队列。

normal.en: Region is the ground that is ruled: the governed area of the same word.
normal.cn: region 是被治理的土地：同一个词的「辖区」。

normal.en: Right and rich are distant cousins: straightness, correctness and power all grow from one root.
normal.cn: right 与 rich 是远亲：笔直、正确与权力都从同一个根上长出。

abstract.en: Picture reins tied to a whole country: whoever holds them runs the regime.
abstract.cn: 想象缰绳拴在整片国土上：谁握住它，谁就运行这个 regime。

abstract.en: A training regime is the country of your body, ruled for one hour at a time.
abstract.cn: 训练方案是你身体的小国，一次只统治一个小时。

abstract.en: Every regime draws straight lines first: through budgets, timetables and habits.
abstract.cn: 每个 regime 都先画直线：穿过预算、课表和习惯。

examples.en: The army took over and a military regime was installed.
examples.cn: 军队接管，一个军事政权建立了。

examples.en: Under the new tax regime, small firms pay less.
examples.cn: 在新税制下，小企业缴税更少。

examples.en: Her doctors designed a gentle regime of rest and medicine.
examples.cn: 医生们为她设计了一套温和的休养服药方案。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞吉姆」——瑞福天天按「日程表」执行统治般的作息 → regime 政权；管理体制；养生方案（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 regimen「统治、驾驭」（regere 引直、统治），核心是「握缰引直之手」，既指治国，也指治身。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of regime, one hand seen at two reins: the reins of a state, of an industry, and of one's own body.
sensesIntro.cn: regime 的四个义项是同一只手握着的几副缰绳：国家的、行业的，以及自己身体的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand holding reins, keeping what it rules on a straight line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只握着缰绳的手，把所治之物保持在线上。

chain: APPLY THE HAND TO THE BODY

branches.en: THE STATE: the government itself and the manner and period of its ruling.
branches.cn: 国家：政府本身及其执政的方式与时期。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: any managed domain — taxes, licences, factories — runs like a small state.
branches.cn: 体系：任何受管领域——税、执照、工厂——都像一个小国般运转。

branches.en: THE BODY: diet and training rules are the reins held over oneself.
branches.cn: 身体：饮食与训练规则是握在自己身上的缰绳。

branches.en: SCALE: the same straightening hand governs a country and a company's paperwork.
branches.cn: 尺度：同一只引直之手既治一国，也治一纸公文。

branches.en: TIME: both the style of rule and the daily routine run on a fixed schedule.
branches.cn: 时间：执政风格与日常作息都按固定节拍运转。

intro.en: Regime carries the Latin stem regere 'to rule, keep straight'. The family fills a page of English: regulate, regulator, regular, region, regent, regimen and regiment all descend from it.
intro.cn: regime 带有拉丁词干 regere「统治、保持笔直」。这个词族在英语中占满一页：regulate、regulator、regular、region、regent、regimen、regiment 都出自它。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is regimen 'steering, rule', from regere 'to keep straight, guide'. Regere also gives regula 'straight bar', the ancestor of rule and regular.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语源头是 regimen「驾驭、统治」，出自 regere「保持笔直、引导」。regere 还派生 regula「直杆」，即 rule 与 regular 的祖先。

items.meaning: a system of rule; a planned routine
items.meaningCN: 政权；体制；养生方案（regere 统治 + -men 结果名词）
items.example: The regime tightened press control.
items.exampleCN: 该政权收紧了新闻管控。

items.meaning: a prescribed course of diet or treatment
items.meaningCN: 养生法；疗程（强调规则本身）
items.example: Stick to the prescribed regimen for two weeks.
items.exampleCN: 遵医嘱的疗程坚持两周。

items.meaning: a military unit; to rule too strictly
items.meaningCN: 军团；过度管束（-ment 构成名词）
items.example: He hated being regimented even on holiday.
items.exampleCN: 即使在假期他也受不了被严格管制。

items.meaning: to control by rule
items.meaningCN: 管制；调节（regula 直杆 + -ate 动词）
items.example: The agency regulates food safety.
items.exampleCN: 该机构负责食品安全监管。

items.meaning: a device or official that keeps a system steady
items.meaningCN: 调节器；监管者（-or 表示装置或人员）
items.example: The pressure regulator keeps the boiler safe.
items.exampleCN: 调压器保障锅炉安全。

items.meaning: following a rule; happening at even intervals
items.meaningCN: 规律的；定期的（regula 规则 + -ar）
items.example: He is a regular at that noodle shop.
items.exampleCN: 他是那家面馆的常客。

items.meaning: a large governed area of land
items.meaningCN: 地区；区域（被治理的地域）
items.example: The region grows most of the country's tea.
items.exampleCN: 该地区出产全国大部分茶叶。

items.meaning: one who rules on a monarch's behalf
items.meaningCN: 摄政者（-ent 表示施动者）
items.example: The queen mother acted as regent for years.
items.exampleCN: 太后摄政多年。

items.meaning: an official rule; the act of controlling
items.meaningCN: 规章；管制（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: New regulations limit truck weights.
items.exampleCN: 新规章限制卡车载重。

items.meaning: having the job of controlling by rules
items.meaningCN: 监管的；规章的（-ory 表示职能）
items.example: A regulatory body reviews the bank's accounts.
items.exampleCN: 监管机构审查银行账目。

latinEntries.meaning: to rule, to keep straight, to guide

definition_zh: 地区；区域；地带；行政区；领域；（身体的）部位；（数值的）大约范围
definition_en: a broad area of land or space, an administrative division, a field of activity, or an approximate range
core_image: 一条线在地上画出的圈：圈内是一片地，圈外是别的世界
scene: 火车穿过山口之后，窗外的语言、屋顶和葡萄品种都变了。The conductor said that they had entered another region, where the roofs and the grapes looked nothing like the ones at home.
sceneCN: 这里 region 是「地理区域」（第 2 个义项：世界或国土的一部分）；句意：列车员说他们已经进入另一个区域，那里的屋顶和葡萄都跟家乡完全不一样。场景要点：山口隧道、车窗外变换的屋顶样式、葡萄园、站牌上的地名。

pos.zh: 地区；区域；行政区；领域；部位

derivatives.zh: 地区的；区域性的；地方性的
在地区层面；按地区
地方主义；区域特色
按地区划分；使区域化
亚区；分区

senses.title: A broad tract of land
senses.definition: a broad area of land whose boundaries are not precisely fixed
senses.definitionCN: 一大片土地，其边界并不精确固定
senses.example: The northern region is mostly forest and thin soil.
senses.exampleCN: 北部地区主要是森林和贫瘠的土壤。
senses.why: Latin regio came from regere 'to direct, rule', and originally named a line or boundary. A region is land that has been marked off, even if the mark is only approximate.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 regio 来自 regere“引导、统治”，最初指一条线或边界。region 就是被划出来的一片地，即使那条线只是大致的。

senses.title: A part of the world
senses.definition: a part of the world or of a country, usually identified by climate, culture, or position
senses.definitionCN: 世界或国家的一个部分，通常以气候、文化或位置来识别
senses.example: Coffee grows best in tropical regions with steady rain.
senses.exampleCN: 咖啡在雨水稳定的热带地区长得最好。
senses.why: The bounded tract is scaled up to the map. Once the line is drawn on a map, the land inside is a region, and neighbouring regions acquire different climates and customs.
senses.whyCN: 被划出的地块放大到了地图上。一旦线被画在地图上，圈内的土地就是一个 region，相邻的区域也获得了不同的气候与习俗。

senses.title: An administrative division
senses.definition: a named administrative division of a country, with its own government or offices
senses.definitionCN: 国家的一个有名行政区划，拥有自己的政府或机构
senses.example: The region of Campania has its own governor and budget.
senses.exampleCN: 坎帕尼亚大区有自己的行政长官和预算。
senses.why: Here the boundary is legal rather than natural. The line is drawn by an authority, which is exactly what the root regere 'to rule' implies: the ruler's line makes the region.
senses.whyCN: 这里的边界是法律的，而不是自然的。线由权威画出，这正是词根 regere“统治”所暗示的：统治者的线造出了区域。

senses.title: The countryside around a city
senses.definition: the rural area lying around a city, used in contrast with the city itself
senses.definitionCN: 环绕城市的那片乡村地带，与城市本身相对
senses.example: The old nobility still owned estates in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 旧贵族仍在这一带拥有庄园。
senses.why: From the late 14th century the word also named the land outside the walls. The city is the centre, and the region is the ring of fields and villages around it.
senses.whyCN: 从 14 世纪晚期起，这个词也指城墙之外的土地。城市是中心，region 就是环绕它的那一圈田野与村庄。

senses.title: A part of the body
senses.definition: a defined part or zone of the body, especially in anatomy and medicine
senses.definitionCN: 身体的一个确定部位或区域，尤用于解剖学与医学
senses.example: The surgeon worked on the lumbar region of the spine.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生在脊柱的腰部区域动手术。
senses.why: The line that marks off land is redrawn on the body. Anatomy divides the body into named regions, so the same word for a bounded tract now names a bounded part.
senses.whyCN: 划出土地的那条线被重新画在身体上。解剖学把身体分成有名字的区域，于是同一个表示“被划出的地块”的词，现在命名一个被划出的部位。

senses.title: A sphere of activity or thought
senses.definition: a field of activity, knowledge, or thought with its own boundaries
senses.definitionCN: 活动、知识或思想的一个领域，有自己的边界
senses.example: That question lies outside the region of physics.
senses.exampleCN: 那个问题落在物理学的领域之外。
senses.why: The boundary becomes invisible. What separates physics from poetry is not a fence but a limit of method, yet the mind still pictures a territory with an inside and an outside.
senses.whyCN: 边界变得看不见了。把物理学与诗歌分开的不是篱笆，而是方法的界限，但头脑仍然把它想象成一块有内有外的领地。

senses.title: An approximate range of a number
senses.definition: in the phrase in the region of, approximately or about a particular amount
senses.definitionCN: 用于 in the region of 这一短语，表示大约、在某个数量左右
senses.example: The repairs will cost in the region of ten thousand pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 维修费用大约在一万英镑左右。
senses.why: The bounded area becomes a bounded interval on a scale. A number 'in the region of' ten thousand is not exactly ten thousand; it is somewhere inside that neighbourhood.
senses.whyCN: 「某一范围」也可以表示大约的数量：介于两个界限之间，就像一大片区域围出的空间，引申为「约数」。英语里 in the region of 就是这个用法。

senses.title: A layer or zone of the atmosphere
senses.definition: one of the horizontal layers or zones of the atmosphere, oceans, or space
senses.definitionCN: 大气、海洋或空间中水平划分的一层或一个带
senses.example: Weather balloons climb into the upper region of the atmosphere.
senses.exampleCN: 气象气球升入大气的高层区域。
senses.why: Height is divided into horizontal bands the way land is divided into tracts. The upper region is not a place with a fence but a layer with a defined range.
senses.whyCN: 高度像土地被分成地块那样，被分成水平的带。高层区域不是有篱笆的地方，而是一个有确定范围的一层。

senses.title: A bounded area in computing
senses.titleCN: 计算机中的一个限定区域
senses.definition: a defined block of memory, or a selected area of a screen or map
senses.definitionCN: 一块被限定的内存区域，或屏幕、地图上被选定的区域
senses.example: The program copies the image into a separate memory region.
senses.exampleCN: 程序把图像复制到一个单独的内存区域。
senses.why: Software needs edges even when nothing physical is being divided. A memory region is a range with a start and an end, the same bounded tract expressed as two addresses.
senses.whyCN: 即使没有实体被分割，软件也需要边界。内存区域是一段有起点和终点的范围，也就是同一块被限定的地，用两个地址表达出来。

intro.en: Region looks as if it begins with re-, but it does not: the re- belongs to the root reg-, from Latin regere 'to direct, rule'. The word's core is a line drawn to bound a tract of land. That makes region unlike recover (capere 'take'), require (quaerere 'ask'), research (circare 'go about') and reside (sedere 'sit'), all of which carry a real re- prefix.
intro.cn: region 看起来像以 re- 开头，其实不是：它的 re- 属于词根 reg-，来自拉丁语 regere“引导、统治”。这个词的核心是一条画出来、把一片地围住的线。因此 region 与 recover（capere“拿取”）、require（quaerere“询问”）、research（circare“绕行”）、reside（sedere“坐”）都不同，后四个才带真正的前缀 re-。

items.en: First recorded as regioun, 'tract of land of a considerable but indefinite extent'. It also meant 'a kingdom, country, nation; the people of a country'.
items.cn: 最早记录为 regioun，意为“范围相当大但边界不定的一片土地”，同时也表示“王国、国家、民族；一国的人民”。

items.en: From Anglo-French regioun and Old French region 'land, region, province' (12c.), and directly from Latin regionem, nominative regio.
items.cn: 来自盎格鲁法语 regioun 与古法语 region“土地、地区、省份”（12 世纪），并直接来自拉丁语 regionem（主格 regio）。

items.en: Latin regio meant 'a district, portion of a country, territory; a direction, line; boundary line, limit'. It was a noun of state from the past-participle stem of regere.
items.cn: 拉丁语 regio 意为“区、国家的一部分、领土；方向、直线；边界线、界限”。它是 regere 过去分词词干的性状名词。

items.en: Regere means 'to direct, rule', from PIE *reg- 'move in a straight line', with derivatives meaning 'to direct in a straight line', hence 'to lead, rule'. A straight line is what makes a boundary.
items.cn: regere 意为“引导、统治”，来自原始印欧语 *reg-“沿直线移动”，其派生义为“沿直线引导”，进而表示“带领、统治”。正是直线构成了边界。

items.en: The sense 'a part of the world' appears in the late 14th century, as does 'the rural area around a city'. The word is now both a map unit and a city's hinterland.
items.cn: “世界的一个部分”这一义项出现于 14 世纪晚期，“城市周边的乡村地带”也在同一时期出现。这个词如今既是地图单位，也是城市腹地。

items.en: The phrase in the region of 'about' is recorded from 1961. Regional is from the early 15th century, and subregion from 1830. The Latin root also gives regal, regent, regime, regulate, direct, correct and rectangle.
items.cn: 短语 in the region of“大约”记录于 1961 年。regional 始于 15 世纪早期，subregion 始于 1830 年。同一拉丁词根还给出 regal、regent、regime、regulate、direct、correct、rectangle。

note.en: The first group separates the derived forms from the noun; the second compares the four area words learners mix up. Region is usually a large or officially bounded area, while its re- is part of reg- 'rule', not the prefix of recover, require, research or reside.
note.cn: 第一组把派生形式同名词分开；第二组比较学习者容易混用的四个“区域”词。region 通常指较大或官方划定的区域，而它的 re- 属于 reg-“统治”，不是 recover、require、research、reside 的那个前缀。

entries.definition: relating to a particular region. It describes something belonging to a region, while region names the area itself.
entries.definitionCN: 与某一地区有关的。它描述属于某个地区的事物，而 region 命名这个地区本身。

entries.definition: loyalty to one's own region, or a feature peculiar to it. It is an attitude or a local trait, not the area.
entries.definitionCN: 对本地区的忠诚，或本地区特有的特征。它是一种态度或地方特色，而不是地区本身。

entries.definition: in a regional way or at the regional level. It modifies an action, while region is a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 以地区方式，或在地区层面上。它修饰动作，而 region 是名词。

entries.definition: a smaller division inside a region. The sub- marks a region within a region.
entries.definitionCN: 一个地区内部的更小分区。sub- 标记“区域之中的区域”。

entries.definition: a part of a place or a measured surface. It is the most general word and can be as small as a room; region usually suggests a larger or more defined stretch.
entries.definitionCN: 一个地方的一部分，或一个被测量的表面。它是最通用的词，可以小到一个房间；region 通常暗示更大或更明确的一片。

entries.definition: an official division of a city, country, or organization for administration. It is usually smaller and more precisely defined than a region.
entries.definitionCN: 城市、国家或组织为行政而划分的正式区域。它通常比 region 更小、边界更精确。

entries.definition: an area marked off for a particular purpose, such as a climate zone or a no-parking zone. It stresses function or rule, while region stresses land or extent.
entries.definitionCN: 为特定目的划出的区域，如气候带或禁停区。它强调功能或规则，而 region 强调土地或范围。

entries.definition: a kingdom, or a sphere of activity. It is more literary and more abstract than region, and it comes from a different French source, not from the Latin reg- root.
entries.definitionCN: 王国，或活动的领域。它比 region 更文学化、更抽象，而且来自另一条法语来源，并非拉丁语 reg- 词根。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin regere 'to rule, direct', regio 'a bounded district', the *reg- family, and the five derived forms regional, regionally, regionalism, regionalize and subregion.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 regere“统治、引导”、regio“被划定的区”、*reg- 词族，以及五个派生形式 regional、regionally、regionalism、regionalize、subregion。

normal.en: regere means 'to rule, direct', and a ruler draws straight lines. A region is the land inside one of those lines.
normal.cn: regere 意为“统治、引导”，而统治者画直线。region 就是其中一条线以内的土地。

normal.en: The same *reg- root gives regal, regent, regime, regulate, direct, correct and rectangle — all about straight lines and rule.
normal.cn: 同一 *reg- 词根给出 regal、regent、regime、regulate、direct、correct、rectangle——全都关于直线与统治。

normal.en: Region's re- is not a prefix: it is the start of reg-, so do not link it to recover or reside.
normal.cn: region 的 re- 不是前缀：它是 reg- 的开头，所以不要把它和 recover 或 reside 联系起来。

normal.en: in the region of means 'about': a number inside a small neighbourhood on a scale.
normal.cn: in the region of 意为“大约”：刻度上某个数附近的一小片邻域。

normal.en: Regional is the adjective, regionalism the attitude, and subregion a region inside a region.
normal.cn: regional 是形容词，regionalism 是态度，subregion 是区域内部的区域。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler drawing one straight line across a map. Everything on one side becomes a region; everything on the other side becomes somewhere else.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子在地图上画下一条直线。线这一侧的一切成为一个 region；另一侧的一切成为别处。

abstract.en: The line can be moved from land to the body, to thought, to numbers, to memory: wherever a boundary is drawn, there is a region inside it.
abstract.cn: 这条线可以从土地移到身体、思想、数字与内存：只要画下一条边界，界内就有一个 region。

abstract.en: A region is not the line itself but the inside it creates, which is why the word always implies both an edge and a stretch of ground.
abstract.cn: region 不是线本身，而是线所造成的内部，所以这个词总同时暗示一条边和一片地。

examples.en: The wine is grown in a cool region near the coast.
examples.cn: 这种葡萄酒产自沿海一个凉爽的地区。

examples.en: Damage to that region of the brain can affect speech.
examples.cn: 大脑那个区域受损可能影响言语能力。

examples.en: A new laptop will cost in the region of eight hundred dollars.
examples.cn: 一台新笔记本电脑大约要八百美元。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞金」——瑞金既是一座城，也是一片有名的地区 → region 地区；区域（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 regio“被划定的区”，其词根 regere 意为“引导、统治”，可追溯到原始印欧语 *reg-“沿直线移动”，核心是“用一条线划出来的一片地”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of region, all from one act: drawing a line to bound a stretch. The stretch can be land, a part of the world, a province, a city's hinterland, a body part, a field of thought, a numeric neighbourhood, a layer of air, or a block of memory.
sensesIntro.cn: region 的九个义项都来自同一个动作：画一条线，把一片范围围起来。这片范围可以是土地、世界的一部分、省份、城市腹地、身体部位、思想领域、数值邻域、大气的一层，或一块内存。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight line drawn to enclose a stretch of ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：画下一条直线，把一片地圈在里面。

branches.en: LAND: an indefinite tract, a part of the world, and an administrative province are the same enclosed ground at three scales.
branches.cn: 土地：边界不定的一片地、世界的一部分、行政区划，是同一片被圈起来的土地在三种尺度上。

branches.en: AROUND THE CITY: the line is drawn at the city wall, and the fields outside become the region.
branches.cn: 城市周边：线画在城墙处，墙外的田野就成了 region。

branches.en: THE BODY: anatomy redraws the line inside a person and names the enclosed part.
branches.cn: 身体：解剖学把线画进人体内部，并给被围住的部位命名。

branches.en: THOUGHT: the boundary becomes invisible, marking what a discipline does and does not cover.
branches.cn: 思想：边界变得看不见，标记一门学科涵盖与不涵盖的范围。

branches.en: MEASURED RANGES: a numeric neighbourhood, a layer of atmosphere, and a block of memory are all bounded intervals rather than ground.
branches.cn: 可测的范围：数值邻域、大气的一层、一块内存，都是有界的区间，而不是土地。

intro.en: Region is not re- plus a root; it is the Latin stem reg- plus -ion. English adds -al, -ly, -ism, -ize and sub-. The same reg- root also supplies regal, regent, regime, regulate, direct, correct and rectangle.
intro.cn: region 不是 re- 加词根，而是拉丁词干 reg- 加 -ion。英语再加 -al、-ly、-ism、-ize 与 sub-。同一 reg- 词根还供应 regal、regent、regime、regulate、direct、correct、rectangle。

latinIntro.en: Latin regere 'to direct, rule' gives the noun regio 'a district, boundary line', the noun rex 'king', and the noun regula 'rule, straight stick'. The PIE root *reg- means 'move in a straight line', which links ruling to drawing a straight boundary.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 regere“引导、统治”给出名词 regio“区、边界线”、名词 rex“国王”与名词 regula“规则、直尺”。原始印欧语词根 *reg- 意为“沿直线移动”，把“统治”与“画一条笔直的边界”联系起来。

items.meaning: a district bounded by a line
items.meaningCN: 被一条线划定的区域（reg- 引导 + -ion 状态名词）
items.example: The region has been famous for its wool for centuries.
items.exampleCN: 这个地区几百年来以羊毛闻名。

items.meaning: relating to a region
items.meaningCN: 地区的；区域性的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: Regional differences in accent are still strong.
items.exampleCN: 口音的地区差异仍然很明显。

items.meaning: at the level of a region
items.meaningCN: 在地区层面上（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The paper is published regionally, not nationally.
items.exampleCN: 这份报纸在地区发行，而不是全国发行。

items.meaning: loyalty to a region, or a local feature
items.meaningCN: 地方主义；地方特色（-ism 构成主义或特征）
items.example: The novel is full of the regionalism of the northern coast.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说充满北部海岸的地方特色。

items.meaning: to organize something by region
items.meaningCN: 按地区组织；使区域化（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The company regionalized its supply chain last year.
items.exampleCN: 公司去年把供应链按地区重新组织。

items.meaning: a smaller division within a region
items.meaningCN: 亚区；分区（sub- 在下 + region）
items.example: Each subregion has a different rainfall pattern.
items.exampleCN: 每个分区都有不同的降雨模式。

items.meaning: belonging to a king or queen
items.meaningCN: 王室的；帝王般的（reg- 王 + -al 形容词）
items.example: The hall was decorated in regal red and gold.
items.exampleCN: 大厅以帝王般的红金两色装饰。

items.meaning: a person who rules during a monarch's absence or minority
items.meaningCN: 摄政者（reg- 统治 + -ent 行为者）
items.example: A regent governed the country while the king was abroad.
items.exampleCN: 国王出国期间由一位摄政者治理国家。

items.meaning: to control by rules
items.meaningCN: 管理；调节（regula 规则、直尺 + -ate 动词）
items.example: The agency regulates the safety of new drugs.
items.exampleCN: 该机构监管新药的安全。

items.meaning: to guide or manage
items.meaningCN: 指导；导演（dis- + regere 使变直）
items.example: She directed the whole production herself.
items.exampleCN: 整场制作由她亲自执导。

items.meaning: to make right or accurate
items.meaningCN: 改正；正确的（com- 共同 + regere 使直）
items.example: He corrected the spelling on the label.
items.exampleCN: 他改正了标签上的拼写。

items.meaning: a four-sided shape with right angles
items.meaningCN: 长方形；矩形（rect- 直 + angle 角）
items.example: The garden is laid out as a long rectangle.
items.exampleCN: 花园被布置成一个狭长的矩形。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb, from PIE *reg- 'move in a straight line'

definition_zh: 地区的；区域的；地区性的；地方（性）的
definition_en: relating to a particular region of a country or the world, or existing only in one region
core_image: 地图上被圈出来的一大块土地：圈里的事在圈里发生，圈外各有各的圈
scene: 周末市集上，北边山城带来的苹果总要早熟半个月，风味也不同。Regional differences in climate shape the fruit harvest.
sceneCN: 这里 regional 是「地区的；区域性的」（第 1 个义项：属于某一地区的）；句意：各区域的气候差异塑造了果实的收成。场景要点：摊位上的苹果、地图与价牌。

pos.zh: 地区的；区域的；地区性的；局部的

derivatives.zh: 同根名词，义为「地区；区域；范围」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「地方主义；地区特征；区域主义」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「在地区层面；按地区」
由形容词加动词后缀构成，义为「使按地区划分；使地区化」

senses.title: Of or typical of a region
senses.definition: relating to, or characteristic of, one particular large area of a country or continent
senses.definitionCN: 与某个国家或大陆的一大块地区相关，或为其所特有
senses.example: Regional dialects fade fastest in the big coastal cities.
senses.exampleCN: 地区方言在沿海大城市消失得最快。
senses.why: The word simply adds the idea of the drawn boundary: everything inside the circle is regional.
senses.whyCN: 这个词只是加上「画出的边界」之意：圈内的万物都是 regional 的。

senses.title: Limited to one region
senses.definition: existing, operating, or available only within one region and not nationally or globally
senses.definitionCN: 只在一个区域内存续、运营或可用，而非全国或全球性的
senses.example: It is a regional bank with branches in three provinces.
senses.exampleCN: 这是一家区域性银行，在三个省设有分行。
senses.why: The circle now works as a limit: what happens inside does not cross the line.
senses.whyCN: 此时这个圈起的是限制作用：圈内之事不越界。

senses.title: Run by or serving a region
senses.definition: of an organization, office, or facility, operated at the level of a region rather than centrally or locally
senses.definitionCN: 指机构、办公室或设施按地区层级运作，而非中央或基层层面
senses.example: She moved to the firm's regional office in Chengdu.
senses.exampleCN: 她调到了公司在成都的地区办公室。
senses.why: Between the whole country and the single town lies the middle circle: regional is the layer drawn between them.
senses.whyCN: 在整国与小镇之间有个中间圈：regional 就是画在两者之间的那一层。

senses.title: Local in a medical sense
senses.definition: affecting or limited to one part or area of the body, as in regional anaesthesia
senses.definitionCN: 影响或局限于身体某个部位，如 regional anaesthesia
senses.example: The surgeon chose regional anaesthesia instead of a general one.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生选择了局部麻醉而非全身麻醉。
senses.why: The map metaphor shrinks to the body: one district of the flesh is numbed while the rest stays awake.
senses.whyCN: 地图比喻缩到身体上：肉身的一个「辖区」被麻醉，其余保持清醒。

intro.en: Regional is the adjective of region, from Latin regio 'direction, boundary, district', from regere 'to keep straight, rule'. A region was first a line drawn straight across the land; the adjective keeps the drawn line in every use.
intro.cn: regional 是 region 的形容词，region 出自拉丁语 regio「方向、边界、地区」，上溯 regere「保持笔直、统治」。region 起初是画在大地上的一条直线；形容词在每种用法里都保留这条画线。

items.en: The root *h3reg- 'to straighten, direct' underlies both regere and its noun family; right, rule and rich are distant English cousins.
items.cn: 词根 *h3reg-「拉直、引导」同时生出 regere 及其名词家族；right、rule、rich 是英语中的远亲。

items.en: Regio meant 'a direction of the sky or land, a boundary, a district': first the straight line, then the territory it marks off.
items.cn: regio 意为「天或地的一个方向、边界、地区」：先是那条直线，再是直线圈出的地盘。

items.en: Region passes through Old French rejon into English in the thirteenth century with the sense 'land under one rule, district'.
items.cn: region 经古法语 rejon 于十三世纪进入英语，意为「同一统治下的土地、地区」。

items.en: The adjective regional forms in English in the seventeenth century, at first rare, marking things that belong to a district.
items.cn: 形容词 regional 于十七世纪在英语中成形，起初罕见，标记「属于某一地区之物」。

items.en: Modern administration spreads the word: regional governments, railways and headquarters make the middle layer of organisation official.
items.cn: 现代行政使这个词普及：地区政府、铁路与总部让「中间层级」的组织获得了正式名分。

note.en: The first group gathers the regere 'draw the line' family around the district word. The second group compares the adjectives of place, from the street to the globe.
note.cn: 第一组汇集围绕「地区」一词的 regere「画线」词族。第二组比较从街巷到全球的「地点」形容词。

entries.definition: a large area of land marked off by nature or administration. It is the word regional circles.
entries.definitionCN: 由自然或行政划出的大片陆地。regional 所圈画的正是它。

entries.definition: loyalty to one's own region, or a local word and custom. The circle turns into a flag.
entries.definitionCN: 对本地区的忠诚，或地方性词语与风俗。圈变成了旗。

entries.definition: following a rule or even spacing. It keeps the straight bar of regula rather than the drawn district.
entries.definitionCN: 守规则的、间隔均匀的。它保留 regula 的直杆，而非画出的地区。

entries.definition: to control by rule. The straightening hand again, applied to systems.
entries.definitionCN: 用规则管制。又是那只引直之手，这次用在体系上。

entries.definition: a system of ruling. The district is what is ruled; the regime is the ruling.
entries.definitionCN: 统治体系。地区是被治之物，regime 是治理本身。

entries.definition: belonging to a small place, a town or neighbourhood. Local is the smaller circle inside the regional one.
entries.definitionCN: 属于小镇或街区这样的小地方。local 是 regional 里面更小的圈。

entries.definition: of a province, sometimes with a tinge of narrow-mindedness. Provincial draws its line by province.
entries.definitionCN: 省的，有时略带见识短浅之意。provincial 以省画线。

entries.definition: covering the whole country. National is the biggest circle of the same set.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖全国的。national 是同套圆圈里最大的一个。

entries.definition: of a territory or claiming one. It stresses ownership and defence of the marked land.
entries.definitionCN: 领土的；主张领地的。它强调对画线土地的拥有与防卫。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin regere 'to rule, keep straight' behind region, regime, regular and regulate, and the picture of a boundary drawn on the map.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 regere「统治、保持笔直」生出 region、regime、regular、regulate，以及地图上画出的边界图景。

normal.en: Region comes from regere: the ruler's straight line across the land becomes the district.
normal.cn: region 出自 regere：统治者画过大地的那条直线变成了地区。

normal.en: The suffix -al simply means 'of': regional is 'of the region'.
normal.cn: 后缀 -al 只表示「属于」：regional 就是「属于地区的」。

normal.en: Regional, national and local are three circles of the same map.
normal.cn: regional、national、local 是同一张地图上的三个圆圈。

normal.en: Regionalism adds -ism: the circle you were born inside becomes a loyalty.
normal.cn: regionalism 加上 -ism：你出生的那个圈变成一种忠诚。

normal.en: In medicine the circle shrinks: regional anaesthesia numbs only one district of the body.
normal.cn: 在医学里圆圈缩小：局部麻醉只麻木身体的一个「辖区」。

abstract.en: Picture a hand drawing one straight line across a folded map: everything on one side of it shares a fate.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在摊开的地图上画一条直线：线同一侧的一切共享同一种命运。

abstract.en: Every region is a rule made visible: the line you can see is the rule you live inside.
abstract.cn: 每个地区都是一条可见的规则：你看得见的线，就是你生活于其中的规则。

abstract.en: Regional news is what matters inside the circle and nowhere else.
abstract.cn: 地区新闻就是只在这个圈内重要、别处无关的事。

examples.en: The supermarket chain adjusts its stock to regional tastes.
examples.cn: 这家连锁超市根据地区口味调整货品。

examples.en: Regional trains stop at every small town along the valley.
examples.cn: 地区列车在山谷沿线每个小镇都停靠。

examples.en: The regional finals were held in Hangzhou this year.
examples.cn: 今年的区域决赛在杭州举行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞吉恩闹」——瑞福在地图上把「区域」用线一「圈」就「闹」明白了 → regional 地区的；区域的（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 regio「地区、边界」（regere 引直、统治），核心是「被一条线圈出的土地」，形容词只是给这块地加上「属于」的标签。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of regional, all one circle seen four ways: the district itself, the limit it sets, the layer of management it creates, and the small circle drawn on the body.
sensesIntro.cn: regional 的四个义项是同一个圆圈的四种看法：地区本身、它划定的限制、它形成的管理层级，以及画在身体上的小圈。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight line drawn across the land, marking off a district.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条画过大地的直线，圈出一块地区。

chain: SHRINK THE CIRCLE TO THE BODY

branches.en: THE DISTRICT: character and products that belong inside the drawn line.
branches.cn: 地区：属于线内之地的风物与特产。

branches.en: THE LIMIT: banks, dialects and media that stop at the boundary.
branches.cn: 限制：止步于边界的银行、方言与媒体。

branches.en: THE LAYER: offices and services run at the level between town and nation.
branches.cn: 层级：介于城镇与国家之间的办公室与服务。

branches.en: THE BODY: the drawn line becomes the surgeon's outline around one part of the flesh.
branches.cn: 身体：画线变成外科医生围住身体一部分的轮廓。

branches.en: TWO FACES OF ONE CIRCLE: what the line holds together is also what the line holds apart.
branches.cn: 一个圆的两面：线聚拢起来的，也正是线隔开来的。

intro.en: Regional adds the Latin adjective suffix -al to region, the district noun of regere 'to keep straight, rule'. The regere family also gives regular, regulate, regime and regionalism.
intro.cn: regional 在 region——regere「保持笔直、统治」的「地区」名词——上添加拉丁形容词后缀 -al。regere 词族还给出 regular、regulate、regime、regionalism。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is regio 'boundary, direction, district', from regere 'to draw straight, rule'. The line that rules the land becomes the land between the lines.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语源头是 regio「边界、方向、地区」，出自 regere「画直、统治」。治理大地的线，变成了线与线之间的土地。

items.meaning: of a region; limited to a region
items.meaningCN: 地区的；区域的（-al 表示「属于」）
items.example: Regional airports link the smaller cities.
items.exampleCN: 区域性机场连接较小的城市。

items.meaning: a large area marked off by nature or rule
items.meaningCN: 地区；区域（-io 构成名词）
items.example: The region is famous for its tea.
items.exampleCN: 该地区以茶叶闻名。

items.meaning: loyalty to one's region; a local feature
items.meaningCN: 地方主义；地区特征（-ism 表示倾向）
items.example: The novel is full of regionalism in its dialogue.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说的对话充满地方色彩。

items.meaning: at the level of a region
